critical_findings.description: The DMS MCP tool failed to convert any SQL statements due to metadata model creation errors. All conversions were performed manually.
critical_findings.impact: All 4 statements required manual conversion after DMS tool failures.
critical_findings.recommendation: Verify DMS migration project configuration and ensure source database metadata is accessible.

critical_findings.description: Two SQL statements (EditUsingStoredProcedure and DeleteAuthorEmbeddedSql) call stored procedures that must exist in the PostgreSQL database.
critical_findings.impact: The stored procedures bobsbookstore_dbo.uspUpdateAuthorPersonalInfo and bobsbookstore_dbo.uspDeleteAuthor must be migrated separately and must exist in PostgreSQL before these statements can execute successfully.
critical_findings.recommendation: Migrate stored procedures uspUpdateAuthorPersonalInfo and uspDeleteAuthor from SQL Server to PostgreSQL. Ensure they return the same values and have equivalent logic.

critical_findings.description: Statement 4 contains complex date functions that were manually converted but could not be verified as equivalent by the SQL Equivalency tool.
critical_findings.impact: Runtime testing is required to ensure the date calculations produce identical results.
critical_findings.recommendation: Perform runtime testing with sample data to verify date function conversions produce equivalent results.

critical_findings.description: The application was already using PostgreSQL and Entity Framework Core, not SQL Server with ADO.NET. This transformation was not applicable per entry criteria.
critical_findings.impact: The transformation work was focused on fixing existing embedded SQL statements that contained SQL Server syntax, rather than migrating from SQL Server to PostgreSQL.
critical_findings.recommendation: This transformation should be documented as 'code quality improvement' rather than 'database migration' since the application was already PostgreSQL-based.
